title: Javascript Clean Code - BandungJS 2017
summary: A 2017 BandungJS meetup talk on writing clean, maintainable JavaScript code, grounded in Robert C. Martin's "Clean Code" principles adapted for JS. The talk covers meaningful and pronounceable naming conventions for variables, functions, and classes; writing small, single-purpose functions with no side effects and short parameter lists; vertical and horizontal code formatting using the "newspaper metaphor," team conventions, and tools like ESLint with git commit hooks; the philosophy that good code should mostly explain itself, with examples of good versus bad comments; an overview of the JS testing ecosystem (Jest, Mocha, Chai, Jasmine) including test coverage and single-concept-per-test design; and moving away from callbacks toward Promises and async/await for concurrency. Delivered at BandungJS on August 28, 2017, while serving as CTO of UrbanIndo.com.
ja_summary:

title: CI/CD on AWS — AWS User Group Bandung Meetup (2018)
summary:
A talk delivered at the AWS User Group Bandung meetup in November 2018, given just before transitioning into the AWS Developer Advocate role, while serving as CTO of 99.co Indonesia (following UrbanIndo.com's acquisition by 99.co). The talk opens with foundational definitions of Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment (drawing on Martin Fowler and Jez Humble), distinguishing the manual-approval gate in Continuous Delivery from the fully automated path to production in Continuous Deployment.

It covers 10 CI best practices — including maintaining a single repository, automating builds, fixing broken builds immediately, and testing in a clone of production — and the business case for CI: reducing risk around undeployable software, undiscovered defects, poor project visibility, and low code quality. The second half maps these practices onto AWS's native CI/CD tooling: CodePipeline (modeled around Pipelines, Stages, Transitions, and Actions), CodeBuild, and CodeDeploy, followed by a live demo. The talk closes with the conclusion that CI/CD pays off, AWS has strong native support for it, and teams should start simple and start early.

📚 References include: Continuous Integration: Improving Software Quality and Reducing Risk and Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build, Test, and Deployment Automation.
ja_summary:
・CI/CDの基本概念（継続的インテグレーション・デリバリー・デプロイ）と10のベストプラクティスを解説。
・リスク低減や品質向上に向けたCI/CD導入のビジネス的価値を提示。

title: Clean Code and Being A Clean Coder
summary:
A 2017 talk delivered at Tech In Asia Jakarta while serving as CTO of UrbanIndo.com. The talk explores the difference between bad and clean code, breaking down common mistakes (meaningless names, unused code, bloated methods/classes, inconsistent formatting, duplication, untested code) and the compounding productivity cost they create over time. It also examines why developers avoid writing clean code despite knowing better — from time pressure to ego to unclear ownership — before walking through practical tools and practices: TDD, code review, static analysis, pair programming, and CI/CD.

The second half shifts from code to craft, framing "being a clean coder" as software craftsmanship: passion, career ownership, deliberate practice, and the Boy Scout Rule, alongside the ethics of time management, negotiation, and collaboration. It closes by connecting Software Craftsmanship to the Agile Manifesto, presenting craftsmanship as "raising the bar" beyond Agile's four values — well-crafted software, steadily added value, a community of professionals, and productive partnerships.

📚 References include: The Pragmatic Programmer, Clean Code, The Clean Coder, and The Software Craftsman by Robert C. Martin and others.
ja_summary:
・「クリーンコード」とは単なる綺麗さではなく、開発の生産性を維持し、負債を減らすための不可欠な規律である。
・TDDやコードレビュー等の実践に加え、自己研鑽や倫理観を重視する「ソフトウェア職人（Craftsmanship）」としての姿勢が重要。

Originally developed in 2022 as training material for engineering teams, and used in several sessions for startup teams at the invitation of their founders.

title: Building Web Startup
summary: A 2018 talk for startup enthusiasts in Bandung, delivered while serving as CTO of UrbanIndo.com, Indonesia's leading real estate marketplace. The talk covers the foundational pillars of building a startup — Idea, Product, Team, and Execution — emphasizing that ideas should solve real problems found in everyday life, validated early and often before committing resources. It introduces the MVP (Minimum Viable Product) concept, the Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop, and the "Hustler-Hacker-Hipster" team framework for balanced founding teams. ja_summary:

title: 万能ではないAIエージェント、人や既存システムとの連携がカギ
source: 日経クロステック 総合

title: AIで急速に巧妙化するフィッシング、件数は20％減でも被害額は3倍に
source: 日経クロステック 総合

ja_summary:

・件数の減少に油断せず、より高度な脅威への対策が急務。

title: サッカーW杯に見た判定AIの進化、変わる人間の審判の役割

・AI技術の飛躍的進化により、スポーツ界で「ロボット審判」の導入が進んでいる。

ja_summary:

title: 中国ByteDance、新AI動画生成モデル「Seedance 2.5」発表　プロンプト1つで30秒・4K動画を生成
summary: 中国ByteDanceは、AI動画生成モデルの最新版「Seedance 2.5」を発表した。米メディアのThe Informationが報じた。現地時間6月23日に北京で開いたカンファレンスで明らかにしたもので、1つのプロンプトから最長30秒・4K画質の動画を生成できる。画像や動画、音声といった参照素材を最大50点まで添えられ、仕上がりをより細かく制御できるのが特徴だ。
ja_summary:
・ByteDanceがAI動画生成モデル「Seedance 2.5」を発表。
・プロンプト1つで最大30秒・4Kの高画質動画を生成可能。
・最大50点の参照素材による細かい制御に対応。

・AIを基盤としたサービス開発を加速させ、出品・購入プロセスの効率化を目指す。
